name: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting and Planning (LATS)
authors: Andy Zhou, Kai Yan, Michal Shlapentokh-Rothman, Haohan Wang, Yu-Xiong Wang (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Lapis Labs)
venue: ICML 2024 (Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:62138-62160). First arXiv submission October 2023 (arXiv:2310.04406).
reflection_type: search-guided (Monte Carlo Tree Search over actions) combined with verbal-self-critique. The LM is repurposed as agent, state evaluator (LM-powered value function), and feedback generator; on unsuccessful terminal nodes it produces a verbal self-reflection used as added context in later trials.
feedback_source: external-tool / environment-reward (environment observations: compiler + LM-generated test-suite results for code, search-API retrieval for QA, browser feedback for WebShop) plus self-generated verbal self-reflection. HotpotQA uses an oracle setup that signals answer correctness; programming uses test-pass percentage as reward.
iteration_structure: tree/MCTS-search. A variant of MCTS runs over k trajectories with six operations performed in succession (selection, expansion, evaluation, simulation, backpropagation, reflection) until the task succeeds or the compute budget is reached.
reflection_object: Primarily the action trajectory (and reasoning chain within it): MCTS searches over a tree whose nodes are states [input, action sequence, observation sequence]. On failure, a verbal self-reflection summarizing errors and proposing better alternatives is generated and injected as context (prompt/context augmentation) for subsequent trials and for the value function. No model weights are modified.
requires_training: none (training-free / gradient-free; the LM-powered value function and reflection both rely on in-context learning, explicitly avoiding the cost of training a value function or RL).
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge: a self-generated LM value function V(s) = lambda*LM(s) + (1-lambda)*SC(s), combining an LM-produced scalar score (after seeing environmental feedback) with a self-consistency heuristic. Augmented by environment/test/oracle reward signals backpropagated through the tree. No separately trained reward model.
distillation_target: episodic-memory: failed trajectories and their verbal self-reflections are stored in a long-term memory structure and re-injected as context in later iterations. The reflections act as a 'semantic gradient' rather than being distilled into model weights or a reusable skill library.
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered. Reflection and the value function are explicitly prompted/orchestrated by the LATS scaffold (MCTS operations + Reflexion-style self-reflection prompts) over a frozen base LM (GPT-3.5/GPT-4); not an RL-emergent reflective behavior.
memory_type: long-term-episodic (external long-term memory storing the search tree, failed trajectories, and self-reflections) plus a short-term scratchpad within a trajectory.
memory_persistence: within-episode / cross-trial within a single task instance: the tree and reflections persist across the k trajectories of solving one task, but memory is not carried across distinct tasks or sessions (the agent is re-initialized per task).
memory_curation_mechanism: append-only with value-guided retrieval: failed trajectories and reflections are appended to memory, and the MCTS value/UCT scores prioritize (gate) which nodes are expanded and which reflections are surfaced as context; no explicit summarization or eviction is described.
error_localization_granularity: step-level / trajectory-level. MCTS operates at the granularity of individual actions/states (each tree node is one action+observation step) so it can revert to and re-expand specific intermediate states; reflection itself is holistic over a failed trajectory (whole-trajectory verbal critique).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task: LATS refines exploration within a single task instance via repeated trajectories, reflections, and tree search; experience is not transferred across separate tasks.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery and avoidance: MCTS can revert to an earlier state and explore alternative branches in-flight (recovery via backtracking), while self-reflection on a failed terminal node is used to avoid repeating the same error in subsequent trajectories.
task_domains: code (program synthesis), QA/reasoning (multi-hop QA), web-navigation (online shopping), math/decision-making (Game of 24).
benchmarks: HumanEval, MBPP (programming); HotpotQA (multi-hop QA, 100-question subset, oracle feedback); WebShop (web navigation, 50 instructions); Game of 24 (math reasoning).
headline_result: State-of-the-art 92.7% Pass@1 on HumanEval with GPT-4 (vs Reflexion 91.0, base GPT-4 80.1). With GPT-3.5: 83.8 Pass@1 on HumanEval and 81.1 on MBPP; 0.71 EM on HotpotQA (CoT+ReAct); 75.9 average score / 38.0% success on WebShop (gradient-free, comparable to gradient-based fine-tuning); 0.44 success on Game of 24.
baselines: CoT, CoT-SC, ReAct, Reflexion, Tree-of-Thoughts (ToT), Reasoning-via-Planning (RAP), plus ToT/RAP adapted with ReAct prompting; on WebShop also imitation learning (IL), IL+RL, and supervised fine-tuning, and human expert performance.
gains_vs_baseline: HumanEval GPT-4: +1.7 Pass@1 over Reflexion (92.7 vs 91.0). HumanEval GPT-3.5: +15.7 over Reflexion (83.8 vs 68.1). MBPP GPT-3.5: +9.7 over RAP (81.1 vs 71.4). HotpotQA: best LATS (CoT+ReAct) 0.71 vs RAP(ReAct) 0.54 (+0.17) and Reflexion 0.51 (+0.20); roughly doubles ReAct (0.32 -> 0.63/0.71). WebShop: +11.7 score over Reflexion (75.9 vs 64.2) and +22.1 over base ReAct (raises average score by 22.1 with GPT-3.5); exceeds RL fine-tuning on score (75.9 vs 67.5). Game of 24: 0.44 vs RAP 0.40 (+0.04).
compute_cost_profile: Higher inference cost than single-pass methods: samples n actions per expansion over k trajectories (sample complexity O(kn) for tree-search variants, same asymptotic order as ToT/RAP). On HotpotQA (n=5, k=50) LATS consumed ~173,290 tokens upon success vs RAP ~176,500 and ToT ~210,215, i.e. LATS expands fewer nodes per success (e.g. 66.65 nodes at k=50 vs RAP 70.60, ToT 84.05; on average 3.55 fewer nodes than RAP and 12.12 fewer than ToT). No training/gradient cost. Authors flag higher compute vs ReAct/Reflexion as a key limitation.
known_limitations: Two stated main limitations: (1) higher computational/inference cost than simpler prompting (ReAct, Reflexion), limiting practicality; (2) it assumes the ability to revert to earlier states in the environment, which is not universally applicable. Additionally, self-reflection gave only a small +0.05 gain on HotpotQA (vs Reflexion's +0.19 over ReAct), and on WebShop reflections were often generic/unhelpful, causing the agent to get stuck in local minima; gains depend on availability of high-quality external feedback.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier and (for some settings) oracle-label/env-reward. LATS is explicitly designed for and depends on external feedback: compiler+test-suite results (code), search-API observations (QA), and browser feedback (WebShop). HotpotQA uses an oracle that signals answer correctness. The paper argues, citing Huang et al. (2024), that LMs cannot reliably self-correct internal reasoning, making external feedback critical.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive but feedback-dependent / task-dependent. LATS improves over all baselines when high-quality external feedback is available (large gains in code and oracle-QA), but the self-reflection component alone contributes only marginally on HotpotQA (+0.05) and is largely unhelpful on WebShop (generic reflections, local minima); most of the gain comes from MCTS search plus external feedback rather than from self-reflection in isolation.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not report confidence-calibration / overconfidence metrics; it focuses on task accuracy/success and token cost).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (LATS is a search+reflection method, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis system; it generates verbal critiques of failed trajectories but does not classify failure modes against a taxonomy or attribute responsibility across agents).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets compounding/propagating errors of autoregressive single-trajectory prompting (CoT/ReAct), lack of exploration of alternative continuations, and inability to incorporate external feedback (hallucination, getting stuck in local minima). Relative to MAST-style modes, it most directly addresses error-propagation/error-loops and superficial single-trajectory reasoning by enabling backtracking and reflection; it does not address multi-agent coordination modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset or benchmark released. The authors released official code, prompts, and model outputs at https://github.com/lapisrocks/LanguageAgentTreeSearch (evaluation uses existing benchmarks HumanEval, MBPP, HotpotQA, WebShop, Game of 24).
builds_on: Monte Carlo Tree Search / UCT (Kocsis & Szepesvari 2006; AlphaGo/AlphaZero, Silver et al. 2016/2017); ReAct (Yao et al. 2023b); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023); Tree-of-Thoughts (Yao et al. 2023a); Reasoning-via-Planning RAP (Hao et al. 2023); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023); Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al. 2022) and Self-Consistency (Wang et al. 2022).
extended_by_or_inspired: Widely cited as a representative MCTS+LLM agent/tree-search method; influenced subsequent LLM tree-search and reasoning works such as Tree Search for Language Model Agents (Koh et al. 2024), AlphaMath / MCTS-for-LLM reasoning lines, RAP-style planners, ReST-MCTS*, and LangGraph's LATS reference implementation. Frequently used as a baseline in later deliberate-search / self-improving agent papers (2024-2025).
reasoning_model_native: No. LATS targets standard (non-reasoning) instruction-tuned LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) and externally scaffolds System-2 deliberation via MCTS+reflection; it predates and does not assume o1/R1-style models with built-in reflection (though the authors frame it as a 'System-2' approach whose value may shift as inference compute cheapens).
on_policy_distillation_link: Weak/indirect. LATS is gradient-free and distills experience only into in-context episodic memory (failed trajectories + verbal reflections), not into model weights; it is not on-policy distillation, but its self-generated value scores and successful trajectories could serve as a data source for later distillation/RL pipelines (a direction other works pursue rather than LATS itself).
sample_efficiency: On HotpotQA, n=5/k=50 reaches 0.63 EM; increasing n improves performance at higher cost. LATS reaches success with fewer expanded nodes than ToT/RAP at matched k (e.g. 66.65 vs 70.60/84.05 nodes at k=50). Programming uses k=8 iterations with n=5 solutions; WebShop/Game-of-24 use k=30, n=5. Same O(kn) sample complexity as other tree-search methods but more sample-efficient per success.
